title: All page content should sit inside landmarks
summary: Some content sits outside any landmark such as header, main or footer. Wrap it in the right landmark so screen reader users can find it.
problem: Some visible content is not inside a landmark region such as <header>, <nav>, <main> or <footer>. In the example the closing notice sits after main, so it belongs to no region at all.
whoItAffects: Screen reader users can jump between landmarks to move around a page. Content outside every landmark is skipped by that way of navigating, so they may never reach it, or reach it only after listening to everything else.
steps: Find the content the scan flagged. It is usually a banner, notice, cookie message or block added by a plugin or script.
Decide where it belongs: inside <main> if it is part of the page content, in <header> or <footer> if it is site-wide, or in <aside> if it is supporting material.
Move the markup into that landmark, or change its wrapper element to the right one.
Make sure the page still has only one main, and that header, nav and footer sit outside it.

whyItMatters: This is a recommended practice rather than a WCAG failure. Landmarks act as a table of contents for people using assistive technology, and content outside them is easy to miss. Notices and cookie banners are the usual cause.
howToCheck: Run a landmarks view in a browser extension, or tab through the page with a screen reader landmark list open. Anything that is not listed under a landmark is outside every region.
